status: local design-system rule; not a physical clearance requirement
scope: visible SVG ink at the palette reference scale; orthogonal candidate ranking has fixed endpoints and boundaries
crossing_count: Count each distinct nonconnected route-pair intersection once using the underlying centerlines before rendering their gaps or bridges; exclude declared connected junctions.
crossing_exception: A deliberate nonconnection crossing may violate parallel-route clearance locally; retain the specified gap or bridge and do not add a junction dot.
hard_constraints: Preserve declared endpoint identities, permitted sides and port direction.
Keep unrelated connectors, label ink, component boundaries and port boxes clear according to the local gaps; only declared endpoints and connected junctions may meet.
A port identifier's annotation leader may touch its own port box; a connection-label leader stops clear of the connection.
An inline label uses a gap in a straight connection, with the specified padding on both sides.
Do not merge independent connections or create unmarked crossings. If no candidate satisfies the constraints, report no feasible candidate.
orthogonal_candidate_rank: shorter total Manhattan length measured in integer candidate-grid ticks
lexicographically smaller ordered list of route vertices, comparing x then y in integer grid ticks
stable_order: For multiple connections, process stable uppercase zero-padded connection IDs in ASCII order; for each fixed-endpoint route compare candidate rank in order. Preserve any explicitly locked routing order. Use the drawing's fixed grid origin; do not snap endpoints that do not lie on the grid, and report them as unsupported for this candidate rule.
scope_limit: Ranking is a deterministic choice among supplied feasible orthogonal candidates; this does not implement a router or prove a global minimum. Curved routes need a separately defined length and bend policy.
